chunks: From him, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who was riding on a beast, and he pressed upon a man who was walking until he was close to trampling him. So the pedestrian drove the beast away from himself, and the rider fell from it and was struck by death or injury. He عليه السلام said: “The one who drove it away is not liable; he only drove it away from himself.”

key_terms.بِضَامِنٍ: legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.فَزَجَرَ: so he drove away or rebuked forcefully

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if he pushes away an animal to protect himself and the rider is injured?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a person who wards off immediate harm from himself is not liable if the aggressor is injured as a result. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies that self-protection in such a case does not make the defender a guarantor of death or injury.
